text: I'm Will Brown. I lead applied research at Prime Intellect, and hope you are all having a great AI Engineer Conference. This is always one of my favorites. It's always just so cool to see what everyone's working on and building, and I feel like it is a place where people get to talk about what the future looks like and, like, start seeing the trends in the industry and seeing the progress and what works and what doesn't. And that's kind of the theme I want to think about for this talk today, is, like, what comes next from what we're doing right now, and what are some of the things that we've been working on and also just been seeing in research that's unfolding that kind of points at what we think the future of AI might look like at the organization level. Because we've seen a lot of very cool progress in agents and interfaces and bots and things like that over the past several months, years. But there's always, like, there's always more coming. Things are just moving so fast, and I think it's a very exciting time to just imagine and speculate and plan for what comes next. And so I don't know if any of you remember back in the early ChatGPT days, OpenAI had kind of spelled out their framing of, like, what are the different stages of AI progress on the road to AGI. And I think we've moved along this faster than we thought we would. We, like, I remember 18 months ago, I was here in New York at AI Engineer giving a talk where we had gotten reasoners and chatbots had been around for a while, and reasoners were, like, the new thing, but we didn't really have agents yet. And now we've climbed pretty quickly through agents and innovators and— The question next seems to be, okay, what happens for organizations? Like, what does it mean for an organization to truly, like, be AI native, not just as, like, a startup that uses a lot of agents and builds everything with cloud code, but, like, at the, like, large enterprise scale? What do companies of the future look like that involve, like, deep integration of agents throughout the lifecycle of the organization? And what do we need to build on the path there? So, a bit about Prime Intellect, just for some backdrop. We build a lot of different things around AI infrastructure for training, deploying, continuously improving models, and especially open source models and open source tooling. And so we do a lot of things, and, like, we roughly do the sorts of things that you would do inside of a big lab. And these are our products. And the reason we do this is because we are imagining a future that is coming pretty quickly, it seems, where open source models are readily available to train and deploy on your own workflows, on your own data, in your own harnesses, and can be the sorts of things that organizations can have grow with them over time, that allow compounding their institutional knowledge, their institutional advantage from their workflows, from their data, from their people and their processes, in addition to using the models from the frontier labs. And so this talk will be a bit about how we see that evolving and unfolding, where, like, what is the role of training in an AI native enterprise? How does this coexist with the frontier models? And, like, what do we think is going to be the version of this that really unlocks the most value for people? And what does it look like? And so organizations have lots of knowledge, and, like, the longer an organization's been around and the kind of more established it is, the more implicit knowledge there is that kind of doesn't ever get written down. There are things that do get written down. There's code bases, there's emails, there's processes. Some of these are very explicit. They're like rules of, like, you must do this, this thing works like that. But a lot of things kind of live in people's heads, and they live in between the lines of the emails, of the meeting notes, of the kind of who talks to who. Like, a lot of companies will have, like, an on-paper org chart and then a real org chart of, like—
